findings.title: Manual retry/sleep loop around auto-reconnecting transport
findings.explanation: NATS and SafeSocket transports maintain internal reconnect buffers and automatic reconnection handlers. Adding manual retry loops causes latency spikes and thread exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: Rely on the transport client's connection lifecycle and error handlers instead of manual retry loops.

findings.title: Mutex guarding atomic primitive operations
findings.explanation: A `sync.Mutex` is being acquired immediately around `atomic.*` load/store operations, paying double synchronization penalties.
findings.recommendation: Rely solely on atomic operations, or replace atomic types with plain types if a mutex is strictly necessary.

findings.title: Check-then-act os.Stat() before os.Open/ReadFile
findings.explanation: Calling `os.Stat` to check file existence before `os.Open` / `os.ReadFile` incurs a redundant disk syscall and creates a TOCTOU race condition.
findings.recommendation: Open/read the file directly and inspect `os.IsNotExist(err)`.

findings.title: Check-then-act disk read (TOCTOU redundancy)
findings.explanation: `exists()` check is immediately followed by `open()` in the branch body. This wastes a stat syscall and introduces a file race condition.
findings.recommendation: Directly attempt to open/read the file and catch `FileNotFoundError` / `OSError` instead.

findings.title: Useless asyncio.Lock in pure synchronous block
findings.explanation: The `async with` critical section contains ZERO `await` yield points. Because Python asyncio is single-threaded, cooperative context switching cannot occur here.
findings.recommendation: Remove `async with self.lock:` to eliminate unnecessary lock acquisition overhead and state complexity.
